newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds close stronger in line with offshore mkts.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds close stronger in line with offshore mkts.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.55 PCT (PREV 7.60) US 5-YR 6.29 (PREV 6.31)
* NZ bonds rally in line with Aust, U.S. markets
* Bills sold at close but rates still seen lower
* Markets to keep close eye on Brash speech on Thursday
New Zealand bonds closed stronger on Wednesday, their yields falling between eight and nine points across the curve primarily on the back of firmer offshore markets, dealers said.
U.S. Treasuries rallied overnight after a speech by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan proved to be less alarming than initially thought, and Australian bonds were also stronger.
"Aussie had a reasonable performance last night...and we've just followed that," said one dealer.
"There's not a great deal happening in the New Zealand bond market at the moment," he added.
In the money market, the 90-day bank bill gave up early gains to close two points higher at 7.38 percent.

"They were pretty much sitting on last night's closes till right on the close, when one of the price makers started giving them out," a bill trader said. "They're two points higher, but there still seems to be a lot of interest to buy."

The New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index remains close to nine-year highs, buoying the short end of the yield curve. One dealer said the 90-days were probably a good 40 points over where they could be with the currency so strong.

The debt markets would closely monitor a speech by Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash on Thursday, but tomorrow's September quarter GDP data was too historical to move the market unless it showed an unexpectedly large fall or rise in growth.
